transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I’ve been… taking on too much. I keep starting things—work plans, certification stuff, projects at home, reaching out to people—and I don’t really stop when I should. It gets intense enough that my wife or my director has had to step in.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
I’m not sure I’d call it impulse exactly. I do things quickly sometimes, but… I usually feel like there’s a reason in the moment. I don’t know. It’s hard to say.
Do you often find it hard to focus on one thing for a long time?

Yeah… sometimes. Little things pull me off. Like if my phone buzzes, or the fan makes a noise, or someone walks by my office, I’ll look up and then I’m not on the report or ticket anymore. I just… lose the thread.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yeah… I do. Sitting still feels kind of wrong sometimes. I’ll get up and pace with my laptop, or start moving things around in the garage. Even trying to just watch a show, I feel like I need to be doing something.
Are these behaviors and feelings causing problems for you at work or in your relationships?

Yeah… it’s caused problems. Work especially. I was put on leave after a migration went badly, and… I guess they didn’t feel I was handling things.

At home, my wife’s had to step in more than I like to admit—around spending, me working late, and conversations turning into arguments.

I’ve also kind of backed out of things I used to do… church music, climbing, mentoring. I just haven’t been reliable enough to show up and follow through.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with focus, restlessness, and taking on too much?
Um… probably about two and a half years. It really started around when I took on that big system migration role at work. Since then it’s just been… harder to manage.
Did you have any of these difficulties with focus, restlessness, or taking on too much when you were a kid?
Not really as a kid, no. This feels more like… the last couple years. Since I took on that big migration role at work—about two years and five months ago.
Do you often experience strong emotions like irritability or anxiety?

Yeah… I do. Some weeks I feel kind of… wired, like I can push through anything. But then if something small happens—like a delay, or my wife asks me a question—I get irritated fast. It feels in the moment like people are trying to slow me down on purpose, even if I know later that’s probably not fair.
Do you experience these feelings of restlessness and difficulty focusing at home as well as at work?

Yeah… it’s at home too. I’ll end up pacing around with my laptop, or suddenly reorganizing the garage, messing with project boards again. If I try to just sit and watch a show, I get… uncomfortable, like I need to be doing something.
Were you more physically active or restless than your peers when you were a child?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I was active like most kids, but I don’t remember being noticeably more restless than everyone else.
Have you noticed any significant impact on your relationships with friends or family members beyond your wife?

Yeah… some. I don’t keep up with people like I used to. I’ve pulled back from church music, climbing, mentoring stuff… I just don’t reliably show up or follow through, so it’s easier to not commit.

And with family, it’s mostly my wife who ends up dealing with it. She’s had to step in around spending, late-night work, and… conversations that turn into arguments. Work’s been affected too—I was put on leave after the migration failed.
Do you experience these feelings of restlessness and difficulty focusing when you're doing things you enjoy, like hobbies?

Yeah… even then. I’ll be trying to work on something I actually like, but if my phone buzzes or the fan clicks, or someone walks past my office door, my attention just jumps there. Then I’ll realize I’ve stopped what I was doing and moved on to something else.
Are there any situations or activities where you feel completely focused and calm, without any restlessness or distraction?

Not really… I mean, sometimes I can settle for a bit, but it doesn’t take much. If my phone buzzes, or the fan clicks, or somebody walks by my office door, my attention just kind of snaps to it. Then I’ve lost the report or ticket I was working on.
Did you have any difficulties in school, such as trouble completing homework or paying attention in class, when you were a kid?
I don’t really remember anything major. I mean, school was a long time ago. I got through it… I don’t think there was anything that stood out like that.
Have you ever found yourself so focused on something that you lost track of time or neglected other things?

Yeah… sometimes. It’s more like I get locked onto a project or a plan and just keep pushing it—work stuff, certification schedules, messing with the home network, even reaching out to people I haven’t talked to in a while. I’ll blow past the point where I should stop, and then my wife or my director has to kind of… pull me back.
Have you experienced these difficulties with focus and restlessness in most areas of your life for the past two and a half years?
Yeah… I’d say pretty much. It’s been going on about two years and five months, I think—since I took on that major system migration role at work.
Have you had times in the past two and a half years where these symptoms significantly improved for a while?

Not really. It’s been pretty steady since I took on that big system migration role at work… about two years and five months ago. Maybe it shifts a little, but I wouldn’t say it really improved for a while.
Have you experienced these difficulties consistently over the past two and a half years, or have there been times when they weren't as problematic?
It’s been pretty consistent, I guess. Since that big system migration role at work… about two years and five months now. There haven’t really been stretches where it wasn’t an issue.
Have you ever been diagnosed with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder or taken any medication for it?
No… not that I know of. I’ve never been told I had that, and I haven’t taken medication for it.
Did you have any symptoms like fidgeting, interrupting others, or blurting out answers when you were a kid?
I don’t really remember that being a thing, no. I mean, I might’ve been restless sometimes like any kid, but I don’t know about interrupting or blurting out answers.
